doc.title: Percy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Films, Lenox and tensions with Milt
title: Bill Evans on the Odds Against Tomorrow soundtrack and other jazz film scores
summary: Heath recalls Bill Evans's calliope part on 'Skating in Central Park' and mentions Miles and Ellington film work.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Now, you made two albums because the actual soundtrack was not MJQ, but it was a larger ensemble and I think it was the first time that John Lewis and all of you guys worked with Bill Evans, the piano player, in that particular setting.
Bill Evans played the calliope on the waltz thing…

“Skating in Central Park” [sings melody]. That was Bill Evans. John wrote that score for horns but that original French score was… I think there was one piece in there, I’m not sure who played it, a blues piece in there, in the film, No Sun in Venice. There’s one thing in there that we didn’t play, I don’t know, but the score for the action and to accompany the scenes, it was all just the four people [of the Modern Jazz Quartet]. And Miles did something like that too for a French movie, and Duke Ellington did something like that, but I think it was all later, and maybe it was incidental music, not the whole score.
Was it “Paris Blues” or something like that?
That was the Duke Ellington with Sidney Poitier and Diahann Carroll in ’61.
Yeah, and that’s when the little hanky-panky was going? [laughs]
